text: Clara took a deep breath, her eyes fixed on the intricate mechanism above. The blades descended with a terrifying whir, but she moved with the precision of a dancer, slipping through the gaps she had memorized down to the millimeter. As the final blade passed inches from her nose, she emerged unscathed, the audience erupting in thunderous applause. Her career was secured, not by luck, but by sheer will and preparation. Meanwhile, the world outside continued its march, unaware that while Clara conquered the stage, history had already claimed the Titanic, the famous ship that sank in 1912 after hitting an iceberg, as a somber reminder of human hubris.
